I farm only 6 mu, so I keep things simple, steady, and practical. I have done wheat-maize rotation for many years, and with my age and my family having some off-farm work, I do not want a management plan that is too complicated or too risky. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to keep both crops stable, especially at key stages, but I still will not over-irrigate because that costs labor and money. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations, and limited pesticide sprays only when needed, because wheat on my land needs stable growth more than fancy inputs. After wheat harvest, I will plant maize on the same 6 mu. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because the yield is usually better and more dependable for me. I will give enough nitrogen for maize since it responds strongly to it, while phosphorus and potassium stay moderate. I prefer rotary tillage because it is easier and fits my small farm better than heavy ploughing, and it is more manageable for me at my age. My goal this year is not to chase the highest possible yield, but to get a reliable harvest from both wheat and maize with inputs I can manage.
